findings.finding: The Sep 28 securities purchase agreement bars the company from any new financing for 30 days after the ~Sep 29 closing, and the ATM was terminated Sep 23. So the usual second shoe for a serial issuer (an ATM draw or offering priced overnight) is contractually unavailable through 2026-10-08, subject to the agreement's unstated 'certain exceptions'.
findings.mechanism_in_window: The restriction covers the whole window (it runs to ~2026-10-29). The fact that lands is that no company supply can price tonight or tomorrow, unlike most serial issuers in the drop universe.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two registered directs (announced after the close on Sep 23 and Sep 28) were followed by +33.07% next close after the Sep 23 fall and -12.45% after the Sep 28 fall (baseline history). So the stock does not react consistently to supply news.
findings.why_not_priced: The base rate for falling serial issuers carries the risk of an overnight offering. The 424B5's no-financing clause removes that tail for this name, and a tape that read it would discount less dilution risk than for an issuer with an open ATM. The effect is small because the clause has exceptions and the stock is falling without any company supply.
findings.independence: The ATM termination supplement is a separate filing pointing the same way: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1907223/000121390026102411/ea0306359-424b5_greenland.htm

findings.finding: About 4.5M shares and pre-funded warrants (~34% of 13.35M outstanding) were sold to institutions at $12 (Sep 23) and $13 (Sep 28). They are registered under S-3, free to trade, and no lock-up binds the purchasers (only officers and directors have a 30-day lock-up). Those holders are ~55% underwater at $5.75 and can keep selling into Oct 8. The March private warrants repriced to $5.00 sit 15% below spot, which adds exercise-and-sell supply on any bounce.
findings.mechanism_in_window: A continuing, undated seller. The shares are tradeable every session with no end date, so the supply behind seven falls in nine sessions is not finished as of today's close.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Since the Sep 23 deal the stock fell from $14.15 (Sep 22 last sale) to $5.75. In the last four falls before today (Sep 29, Oct 1, Oct 2, Oct 6) the next close was +2.36, -13.5, -6.85 and -9.87: three of four continued.
findings.why_not_priced: The price holds the selling so far, not the stock of holders still underwater. Today's 0.34x volume says those holders are not capitulating in size, so the remainder is still to come. If the supply were spent, the fall would have printed on heavy volume at the low. The finding is kept small because the purchasers' remaining positions are not disclosed: this is an inference from the filings, not a counted supply.
findings.independence: The Sep 28 424B5 limits the lock-up to directors and executive officers: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1907223/000121390026104114/ea0306753-424b5_green.htm
